sections.label: 1 · INTAKE
sections.note: Typeform's native trigger fires the instant a response is submitted — no polling, no delay. Fields are mapped once here, so if you ever add a question you change one node and nothing downstream breaks.

sections.label: 2 · GUARD
sections.note: Two cheap checks that stop the two things that actually go wrong in production: a resubmitted form creating a duplicate row, and a blank or malformed response silently landing in the base.

sections.label: 3 · RECORD
sections.note: The Airtable row is the source of truth and is written before anything is announced, so Slack never notifies about a record that failed to save.

sections.label: 4 · NOTIFY
sections.note: A formatted Slack message with the submitter's name and a readable summary, then the Airtable row is stamped so you can see at a glance which submissions were announced.

nodes.label: Map Typeform Answers → Named Fields
nodes.notes: Typeform returns answers as a positional array; this turns them into name, email, company, message.

nodes.label: Build Slack Summary Block
nodes.notes: Truncates long answers and keeps the message readable on mobile.

answers.name: Priya Raghunathan
answers.message: We run three Typeforms for different service lines and everything is being copied into Airtable by hand every morning. Looking to stop that.

slack.text: New Typeform submission — Priya Raghunathan (Lumen Labs) · Budget $2,000–$5,000 · "Three Typeforms copied into Airtable by hand every morning…"
